deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether the TargetServer can be accidentally deleted or removed from Terraform management.

description.description: A human-readable description of this TargetServer.
description.rationale: Provides documentation only and does not affect security behaviour. This is a cosmetic description field.

env_id.description:
The Apigee environment group associated with the Apigee environment,
in the format 'organizations/{{org_name}}/environments/{{env_name}}'.
env_id.rationale: Identifies the deployment environment, and the correct value is organisation-specific. this is a resource identifier/reference.

host.description: The host name this target connects to. Value must be a valid hostname as described by RFC-1123.
host.rationale: Identifies the target host, and the correct value depends on the organisation's architecture. this is a reference/endpoint pointer.

is_enabled.description: Enabling/disabling a TargetServer is useful when TargetServers are used in load balancing configurations, and one or more TargetServers need to taken out of rotation periodically. Defaults to true.
is_enabled.rationale: Controls whether the target server participates in traffic routing and load balancing. This is an operational availability and provisioning decision made by the service team, not a platform-level security control.

name.description: The resource id of this reference. Values must match the regular expression [\w\s-.]+.
name.rationale: Identifies the TargetServer resource and does not directly control security. This is a resource identifier.

port.description: The port number this target connects to on the given host. Value must be between 1 and 65535, inclusive.
port.rationale: Specifies the network port used to connect to the backend service. The appropriate port depends on the team's service architecture and routing configuration, and a port number alone does not determine transport security, so it is not a useful generic platform policy target.

protocol.description: Immutable. The protocol used by this TargetServer. Possible values: ["HTTP", "HTTP2", "GRPC_TARGET", "GRPC", "EXTERNAL_CALLOUT"]
protocol.rationale: Controls the protocol used for communication with the backend target server. A platform policy can restrict the configuration to approved protocols and prevent the use of protocol configurations that permit unencrypted or insufficiently protected backend communication.

s_sl_info.description: Specifies TLS configuration info for this TargetServer. The JSON name is sSLInfo for legacy/backwards compatibility reasons -- Edge originally supported SSL, and the name is still used for TLS configuration.

s_sl_info.ciphers.description: The SSL/TLS cipher suites to be used. For programmable proxies, it must be one of the cipher suite names listed in: http://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/technotes/guides/security/StandardNames.html#ciphersuites. For configurable proxies, it must follow the configuration specified in: https://commondatastorage.googleapis.com/chromium-boringssl-docs/ssl.h.html#Cipher-suite-configuration. This setting has no effect for configurable proxies when negotiating TLS 1.3.
s_sl_info.ciphers.rationale: Controls the cipher suites used to encrypt connections and should exclude weak ciphers.

s_sl_info.client_auth_enabled.rationale: Controls whether mutual TLS is used to authenticate the client.

s_sl_info.enabled.description: Enables TLS. If false, neither one-way nor two-way TLS will be enabled.
s_sl_info.enabled.rationale: Directly controls whether TLS encryption is enabled for the target connection.

s_sl_info.enforce.description: If true, TLS is strictly enforced.
s_sl_info.enforce.rationale: Controls whether TLS is strictly required for the target connection.

s_sl_info.ignore_validation_errors.description: If true, Edge ignores TLS certificate errors. Valid when configuring TLS for target servers and target endpoints, and when configuring virtual hosts that use 2-way TLS. When used with a target endpoint/target server, if the backend system uses SNI and returns a cert with a subject Distinguished Name (DN) that does not match the hostname, there is no way to ignore the error and the connection fails.
s_sl_info.ignore_validation_errors.rationale: Ignoring certificate errors can permit connections to untrusted or impersonated servers.

s_sl_info.key_alias.description: Required if clientAuthEnabled is true. The resource ID for the alias containing the private key and cert.
s_sl_info.key_alias.rationale: Selects the private key and certificate used to authenticate the client when mutual TLS is enabled. This argument references the client certificate key alias used for mutual TLS authentication; a platform policy should require this field to be set (non-empty) to ensure mTLS client authentication is configured, without hardcoding a specific alias name.

s_sl_info.key_store.description: Required if clientAuthEnabled is true. The resource ID of the keystore.
s_sl_info.key_store.rationale: Identifies the keystore containing the client credentials used for mutual TLS. This argument specifies the keystore holding client credentials for mutual TLS; a platform policy should require it to be configured (non-empty) to ensure client authentication credentials are active, while avoiding specific resource naming.

s_sl_info.protocols.description: The TLS versioins to be used.
s_sl_info.protocols.rationale: Controls the permitted TLS versions and should exclude obsolete protocols.

s_sl_info.trust_store.description: The resource ID of the truststore.
s_sl_info.trust_store.rationale: Identifies the trusted certificates used to validate the target server. This argument specifies the truststore for validating backend server certificates; a platform policy should require it to be configured (non-empty) to ensure trust validation is enabled, without pinning specific resource names.

s_sl_info.common_name.description: The TLS Common Name of the certificate.

s_sl_info.common_name.value.description: The TLS Common Name string of the certificate.
s_sl_info.common_name.value.rationale: Specifies the certificate identity expected from the target server. This argument specifies the expected certificate common name for server validation; a platform policy should require it to be non-empty and properly populated to prevent missing hostname validation checks, without pinning a specific target domain.

s_sl_info.common_name.wildcard_match.description: Indicates whether the cert should be matched against as a wildcard cert.
s_sl_info.common_name.wildcard_match.rationale: Controls whether wildcard matching is allowed during target-server certificate validation. A platform policy can require false to enforce strict certificate identity matching and prevent broader wildcard certificate names from being accepted.
